newsitem.title: POLAND: World Bank pledges help for Poland after floods.
newsitem.headline: World Bank pledges help for Poland after floods.

text.p: The World Bank offered Poland broad financial assistance on Wednesday to help rebuild areas damaged by this month's heavy floods.

"We are very willing to provide whatever assistance the government of Poland will require in terms of helping to restore the infrastructure, buildings, houses, which have been damaged by the floods," the bank's director in charge of Poland, Basil Kavalsky, told reporters after a meeting with finance ministry officials.

The finance ministry earlier said it sought a $300 million loan from the bank, and a similar loan from the European Investment Bank (EIB), to help rebuild the southern part of the country, where the floods swamped more than 5,000 square km killing 55 people.
Kavalsky said that before any loan decision was made the bank's mission had to examine the scope of damages and assess assistance needs.
"The first mission will be coming in a week or two to make assessment of the damage and try to see what support the World Bank can offer," he said after meeting deputy finance minister Pawel Samecki.
But Kavalsky encouraged the government to start repairing the infrastructure right away and not to economize too much, saying the bank's future loan would reimburse costs borne now.

"We have given indication that we will be willing to finance some of that (repair cost) retroactively so that the government can proceed with works and we will then come in and reimburse the works," he said.

Kavalsky said the floods were unlikely to cause any significant slow-down of economic growth this year but suggested that inflation might be higher than 13 percent forecast by the government for December.
"Inflation may not come down quite as quickly as had been hoped," he said.
Kavalsky also promised the bank's help in financing the coming reform of the social security system, calling it "one of the key initiatives" since the fall of communism in 1989.
